hero.h1: Sewer Line Drain Cleaning and Rodding in Skokie, IL
hero.sub: When water comes up at the basement floor drain or every drain slows down at once, your main sewer line is blocked. We rod it clear, show you the cause on camera and price it before we start. Our office is on Lincoln Avenue.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber feeding the cable from a drum rodding machine into an outdoor sewer cleanout in a front yard

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Sewer Lines From Skokie's Building Boom
blocks.body: Skokie grew from about 15,000 people in 1950 to nearly 60,000 by 1960. Most homes from that boom still drain through clay laterals laid at the time, now more than 60 years old. Their joints are where roots get in. That's why so many Skokie homeowners have their main line rodded every year or two, and why a camera look after rodding is worth it.

blocks.h2: Sewer Line Cleaning Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: What's the difference between sewer line drain cleaning and rodding?
items.answer: They describe the same service: cutting through roots and clogs in the main line with a motorized cable.

items.q: How often should a Skokie home have the main line cleaned?
items.preview: Yearly if roots are a known problem.
items.answer: If roots have blocked your line before, once a year is common, usually in late winter or early spring.

items.q: Is rodding safe for a 70-year-old clay pipe?
items.preview: Yes, with the right cutter. We camera it after.
items.answer: Yes, with a cutting head sized for the pipe. The camera afterward shows whether the clay is cracked or broken.

items.q: Where is the cleanout in a 1950s Skokie home?
items.preview: Usually in the basement near the front wall.
items.answer: Usually in the basement, near where the line leaves for the street, often by the floor drain. Some homes also have one outside.

items.q: Can rodding fix a line that keeps clogging?
items.preview: It clears it. The camera shows why it clogs.
items.answer: Rodding clears it. The camera shows whether roots, a break or a sag keeps causing it.

items.q: How much does sewer line cleaning cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the cleanout location, the length of the line and what's blocking it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
